 Judgment

The claimant in O.P. (MV) No.580 of 2018, before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Vatakara,
has instituted this appeal seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the order dated 29.02.2020.
The accident occurred on 02.12.2017 when the claimant was aged 26 years.
2. Heard Sri.Zubair Pulikool, the learned counsel for the appellant, as well as Sri.Raji T. Bhaskar, the learned counsel for the insurance company.
3. The first issue arising for consideration is as regards the fixation of the notional income by the Tribunal.

The claimant has pointed out that he was employed in Qatar as a driver, aged 26 years,
and he was earning an amount of Rs.70,000/- per month at the time of the accident.
In support of this, the claimant had relied upon a salary certificate at Ext.A6, which was marked subject to the objection by the Insurance Company.

But a perusal of the award would show that apart from producing the afore salary certificate, the MACA No.296 of 2021 2025:KER:93750 same has not been proven, in accordance with law, by obtaining certification with reference to the provisions of the Diplomatic and Consular Officers (Oaths and Fees) Act, 1948.

entities.text: Diplomatic and Consular Officers (Oaths and Fees) Act, 1948
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In such circumstances, as held by this Court in Satheesan E.K. v. Musthafa K.P. and Another [2018 (5) KHC 884], the salary certificate produced by the claimant cannot be acted upon.

entities.text: Satheesan E.K. v. Musthafa K.P. and Another [2018 (5) KHC 884]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
However, in Satheesan (supra), this Court,
following the earlier judgment in Valsamma and Another v. Binu Jose and Others [2014 (1) KHC 207], has ultimately found that at least 1/4th of the salary can be adopted in such cases.

entities.text: Valsamma and Another v. Binu Jose and Others [2014 (1) KHC 207]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case at hand, also, insofar as only the salary certificate has been produced, there being no certification by the Embassy/Council, I am of the opinion that 1/4th of Rs.70,000/-, amounting to Rs.17,500/- has to be adopted as the notional income.
To that extent, the award of the Tribunal requires to be modified, and I do so.
4. Sri.Zubair would contend that the assessment of the occupational disability of 6% was without any justification.
With reference to the certificate at Ext.A10, this Court notices MACA No.296 of 2021 2025:KER:93750 that the certificate was issued by a solitary doctor and not by a medical board.
Furthermore, the doctor is also not examined.
That being so, much reliance cannot be placed on the disability certificate produced as above.

Furthermore, with reference to the nature of the injuries as noticed by the Tribunal in paragraph 18 of the award, in my opinion, the assessment of the occupational disability at 6% cannot be faulted.
Therefore, I am of the opinion that no further modification requires to be made on that ground.
5. Sri.Zubair, the learned counsel for the appellant, would also point out that, as against pain and suffering, only an amount of Rs.50,000/- has been awarded by the Tribunal.

This, according to him,
is inadequate in comparison to the nature of the injuries.

On a perusal of the nature of the injuries,
as noticed earlier, I am of the opinion that a minor variation needs to be carried out in this regard.
Therefore, compensation against pain and suffering is modified at Rs.70,000/-.

In such circumstances, the appellant would be entitled for the following amounts:

In the result, this appeal is partly allowed, modifying the impugned award, entitling the appellant to get an additional MACA No.296 of 2021 2025:KER:93750 amount of Rs.1,47,680/- (Rupees One Lakh Forty-Seven Thousand Six Hundred and Eighty only), along with the amounts already awarded by the Tribunal, to be paid by the 3rd respondent - Insurance Company.

Needless to say, all other findings and directions of the Tribunal in the impugned award, including the rate of interest,
will remain unaltered.
